S08.title: Reviewed conflict actions (select winner, keep copies, manual merge)
S08.evidence: Web UI provides dedicated modal for reviewed conflict actions with radio selection for winner, dry-run path preview for keep-copies, and content text editor for manual merge. All mutating actions enforce expected_head_token and reviewed version IDs, rejected with 409 STALE_VIEW if concurrent heads change.

S16.title: Qualified status, storage warnings, and unavailable historical content
S16.evidence: Folders view displays qualified per-peer progress (direct receipts only, non-transitive), storage reserve warnings (512 MiB reserve and 256 MiB WAL cap), and files view explicitly differentiates ready, pending, unavailable, and expired content availability states with disabled restore triggers.

S18.title: Automatic agent/shared UI with zero runtime Node dependency
S18.evidence: Embedded React/TypeScript/Vite static assets compiled to dist/ and embedded into the Go binary via //go:embed. Runs entirely self-contained without Node at runtime; browser closing does not stop synchronization.

I16.title: Cross-origin browser requests cannot mutate state or read sensitive data; control endpoints require local authentication
I16.evidence: Loopback server validates Host and Origin headers, serves static assets and session bootstrap, issues HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies and per-session CSRF tokens. Mutating operations mandate X-CSRF-Token headers.

I19.title: Safe recovery preserves user data; UI and CLI use the same control operations
I19.evidence: Web interface routes all state reads and mutations through the exact same /api/v1/... control endpoints as CLI commands. Pending/failed operations never render as successful completion.
